name: Aikibeye
ingredients: Mustard leaves (locally known as mustard greens)
instructions: 1. Peel and slice the colocasia roots into small pieces.
2. Wash and roughly chop the mustard leaves.
3. In a pot, add the colocasia roots with just enough water to cover them and bring to a boil.
4. Once the roots begin to soften, add the chopped mustard leaves and green chilies.
5. Continue boiling over medium heat until both ingredients are tender and most of the water has evaporated.
6. Mash the mixture thoroughly using a wooden spoon or masher to create a thick, cohesive texture.
7. Season with salt to taste and serve hot as a side dish with steamed rice.
description: Aikibeye is a quintessential Naga dish that highlights the simplicity and reliance on local, farm-fresh produce. It is a staple in Sumi Naga households, celebrated for its earthy flavors and the unique creaminess derived from the cooked colocasia roots.
